nodes.content: Investigate whether language models can revise temporal inferences under corrected narratives while preserving uncertainty about underspecified event order.
requirements: Achieve macro-F1 ≥0.85 classifying temporal claims as entailed, contradicted, or undetermined on unseen event structures.
Preserve ≥95% of previously correct temporal judgments unaffected by narrative corrections while updating affected judgments.

nodes.content: Have an LLM extract provenance-tagged temporal constraints, incrementally recompute affected closure after corrections, and classify claims by bidirectional reachability.
Can provenance-tagged closure updates distinguish correction-dependent event orders from genuinely unspecified pairs without changing unrelated judgments?
Provenance-scoped closure will yield ≥0.85 macro-F1, ≥0.85 undetermined-class F1, and ≥95% unaffected-judgment retention on unseen event structures.
Test extraction-and-closure on TempoRev-500 graph-disjoint correction pairs with gold partial orders; measure macro-F1, undetermined F1, retention, and update accuracy.
On TempoRev-500, closure achieved 0.88 macro-F1, 0.86 undetermined F1, 97% unaffected-judgment retention, and 90% corrected-claim update accuracy.
Ablate provenance on held-out TempoRev-500 fork-join corrections; compare undetermined F1, affected-update accuracy, and unaffected-judgment retention against full closure.
On fork-join cases, full closure scored 0.78 undetermined F1, 92% retention, 84% update accuracy; provenance ablation scored 0.66, 81%, 72%.
Adding fork-join incomparability certificates to provenance-scoped closure will yield ≥0.85 undetermined F1, ≥95% unaffected retention, and ≥90% update accuracy.
Implement fork-join incomparability certificates and rerun TempoRev-500’s held-out split, comparing undetermined F1, unaffected retention, and update accuracy.
With incomparability certificates, held-out TempoRev-500 fork-join cases reached 0.87 undetermined F1, 96% unaffected retention, and 91% update accuracy.
Evaluate certificate-guided closure on graph-disjoint TempoRev-Chain-200 three-correction narratives, measuring macro-F1, undetermined F1, unaffected retention, and update accuracy.
On TempoRev-Chain-200, certificate-guided closure scored 0.81 macro-F1, 0.78 undetermined F1, 89% unaffected retention, and 82% update accuracy.
On unseen multi-correction narratives, fork-join certificates alone will yield <0.85 undetermined F1 and <95% unaffected retention.
Add versioned dependency tracking to invalidate superseded constraints, then retest uncertainty and unaffected judgments across sequential corrections.
Calibrate regression checks to e3’s 0.87/96% and e4’s 0.78/89% F1/retention; compare certificate-only and versioned invalidation on new chains.
On held-out TempoRev-Chain-200 chains, certificate-only scored 0.79 undetermined F1 and 90% retention; versioned invalidation scored 0.86 and 96%.
TempoRev-Chain-200 evaluation bundle contains gold partial orders, correction-version dependencies, fork-join certificates, and scripts reporting F1 and retention.
Adopt versioned invalidation with fork-join certificates: certificates succeeded on fork-joins but failed on chains; versioning restored uncertainty and retention.
Fine-tune an LLM with correction-pair contrastive loss, explicit undetermined labels, and consistency regularization on unaffected event pairs.
Can contrastive training teach an LLM to update correction-dependent claims while preserving undetermined orders and unaffected judgments on unseen structures?
Contrastive fine-tuning will reach ≥0.85 macro-F1 and ≥0.85 undetermined F1 while retaining ≥95% unaffected judgments on graph-disjoint corrections.
Audit TempoRev-Chain-200 gold orders and dependencies; test contrastively tuned LLM on graph-disjoint splits for macro-F1, undetermined F1, and retention.
Audit verified gold correction dependencies; on graph-disjoint TempoRev-Chain-200, contrastive LLM achieved 0.86 macro-F1, 0.86 undetermined F1, 96% unaffected retention.
Retain contrastive fine-tuning as a viable alternative: graph-disjoint results meet macro-F1, undetermined F1, and unaffected-retention thresholds.
Use correction-aware evidence retrieval with a temporal NLI verifier and calibrated abstention for event pairs lacking ordering evidence.
Index narrative versions, train the temporal NLI verifier on correction-linked evidence, calibrate abstention, and test graph-disjoint classification and retention.
Using TempoRev-Chain-200’s gold orders and dependencies, test version-filtered retrieval plus calibrated temporal NLI for macro-F1, undetermined F1, and retention.
TempoRev-Retrieve v1 contains version-filtered evidence, temporal NLI predictions, abstention scores, and graph-disjoint F1 and retention reports.
On graph-disjoint TempoRev-Chain-200, version-filtered retrieval and temporal NLI achieved 0.87 macro-F1, 0.88 undetermined F1, and 97% unaffected-judgment retention.
Audit TempoRev-Retrieve v1 provenance; ablate version filtering and abstention on held-out chains, comparing macro-F1, undetermined F1, and retention.
On long-range chains, full retrieval scored 0.82 macro-F1 and 92% retention; removing version filtering lowered macro-F1 to 0.76.
Defer retrieval-only deployment: aggregate scores pass, but long-range chains fall below macro-F1 and retention targets despite version filtering.
Combine versioned constraint closure with contrastive LLM predictions, using graph reachability for long-range order and certificates for undetermined pairs.
Does combining graph reachability with contrastive predictions improve long-range correction handling without misclassifying unlinked event pairs?
On graph-disjoint long-range chains, hybrid closure–LLM inference will achieve ≥0.88 macro-F1, ≥0.85 undetermined F1, and ≥95% unaffected-judgment retention.
Use e7’s aggregate baseline and e8’s long-range failure cases to benchmark hybrid inference on macro-F1, undetermined F1, and retention.
On graph-disjoint long-range chains, hybrid inference reached 0.87 macro-F1, 0.86 undetermined F1, and 94% unaffected-judgment retention.
Gate LLM overrides by correction dependencies; predict ≥0.88 macro-F1, ≥0.85 undetermined F1, and ≥95% retention on long-range chains.
Implement dependency-gated LLM overrides and rerun graph-disjoint long-range chains; measure macro-F1, undetermined F1, unaffected retention, and affected-update accuracy.
Dependency-gated hybrid inference scored 0.89 macro-F1, 0.87 undetermined F1, 97% unaffected retention, and 92% affected-update accuracy on long-range chains.
Test gated hybrid against baselines on unseen topologies with sequential retractions and disconnected pairs; audit uncertainty and retention.
Using e10’s gated hybrid and TempoRev-Retrieve v1, compare methods on unseen retraction/disconnected-pair topologies: macro-F1, undetermined F1, retention.
TempoRev-Retrieve v2 replaces v1’s retrieval-only reports with gated-hybrid comparisons on unseen retractions and disconnected pairs, including F1 and retention.
On unseen long-range retraction/disconnected-pair topologies, gated hybrid achieved 0.90 macro-F1, 0.88 undetermined F1, 97% retention; retrieval achieved 0.83 macro-F1.
Adopt dependency-gated hybrid: gating corrected the initial retention shortfall and met F1 and retention targets on unseen retraction topologies.
Rebuild temporal SAT models after corrections; classify claims using dual satisfiability tests, retaining uncertainty when both orders remain possible.
Encode event constraints as versioned SAT clauses, retract superseded clauses, probe both claim polarities, and compare classification and retention.
Use TempoRev-Retrieve v2 splits and e8’s long-range failures to benchmark versioned SAT against gated hybrid: macro-F1, undetermined F1, retention.
On v2 unseen topologies, versioned SAT achieved 0.86 macro-F1, 0.91 undetermined F1, and 98% unaffected-judgment retention.
TempoSAT-v1 contains versioned temporal clauses, dual-satisfiability claim labels, and v2-split macro-F1, undetermined F1, and retention reports.
Keep versioned SAT for uncertainty audits (0.91 undetermined F1, 98% retention); prefer hybrid’s macro-F1; retain contrastive alternative, defer retrieval.
